actual_file_scope: All 425 lines (17,115 bytes), both proofs and the final scope remark were freshly read. No mathematical or typesetting correction was found.
checks: The affine-curve degree-two comparison gives a same-field GL lift. For a fixed projective local type, all linear lifts differ by one of exactly q-1 local scalar characters; no false injection from projective to linear conjugacy classes is required.

The projective splitting field lies inside that of a linear lift, and the intervening scalar group is prime to p. The exact tower formula gives normalized different d_x+(e_tame-1)/(e_projective*e_tame), hence at most d_x+1. No highest-break inference from a normalized-different bound is made.
The invariant-lattice proof applies directly with c_x=ceil(p(d_x+1)) for all f phases. Its trace-dual calculation is rank-independent and does not divide by a possibly wild group order.

The two actual Frobenius inclusions and their duals give the slope window with the degree Delta of the variable divisor B. The explicit H degree 2g+4+ceil(Delta/(p-1)) makes E_j(H) generated and H1-acyclic; both alternating generating lines in the fixed partial resolution meet the stated degree bounds.

The seven/three separated partial complexes and top-generator identity test compute actual bundle maps and inverse identities. The unit-minor open conditions give local split cancellation over arbitrary coefficient rings.

The uniform line estimate h0+h1<=2g+2+|degree| gives O_p(A r^2) coordinates per phase: top-top multiplicity r^2 has line degree O_p(A), mixed multiplicity r has line degree O_p(rA), and bottom-bottom multiplicity is bounded. No moving determinant or variable cohomology basis is introduced.

The finite Cech contraction has fixed internal width; all polynomial degrees depend only on p. Increasing a jet length increases coefficient slots but not polynomial degree. One-step Frobenius is used, not an expanded q-power identity.

Each branch uses its own N_x and L_x=N_x+c_x, so (p-1)N_x>c_x and the sum of local frame lengths is O_p(Delta+number of marks). The actual all-ring cyclic comparison retains N_x and identifies canonical integral local types.

The specified-Artinian Isom proof retains the fixed full local types. Nilpotent etale invariance and the functorial canonical lattice, followed by completion faithful flatness, justify the proper-curve lift and open class images. Bounded different alone is not used for that step.
The component prefactor is included and is absorbed into p^{O_p(fAr^2)}. The scalar lift tuple factor is also included. Empty fibres and projective rank one cause no exception.
The single original detecting curve pulls back to a connected degree-t curve because its fundamental group surjects onto the original Gamma. The pulled-back fundamental group surjects onto H.

For every finite H representation, its open normal core in Gamma gives one finite Galois quotient simultaneously trivializing the representation and coset cover. Local fields K_y sit in its local Galois splitting field; the size of this core quotient is never charged.
Tower transitivity gives delta_y<=e_y(b_x+1) and exactly delta(L/K_y)/e(L/K_y)=e_y*delta(L/K_x)/e(L/K_x)-delta_y. Passing to the projective quotient decreases normalized different.

The true wild Riemann-Hurwitz formula yields genus plus number of marks O(t), and summing d_y=e_y(b_x+1)-delta_y gives O(t). All local Frobenius and testing depths sum to O(t); the maximum depth is not charged once per mark.

The degrees of the connected cover factors of each fixed complete local puncture sum to t even when its map to Gamma is noninjective. One representation class on such a factor determines every curve branch using it, so each surface factor is counted exactly once.

The local bounded-period hereditary theorem gives q^{O(t r^2)} tuples of local classes; the quantitative fixed-type curve lemma gives the same bound in each fibre. Surjectivity of the original detector yields the required conjugacy-class injection.

At added points outside T the local map to Gamma and all induced local maps are trivial. A global geometric period bound restricts, and the ordinary multiplier is killed by r and q-1. No semilinear transfer or unrestricted local-period conclusion is asserted.
